messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int i = 0;
while (i < 3) { fire(); }

Question: How many shots are fired?
The student answered: 3

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The loop variable advances by itself and the loop ends by itself

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: long-winded, walks through the steps one by one, 20 to 35 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["First i is 0, then after one fire it moves ahead, then second fire, then third fire, and when i reaches 3 it stops.", "The while checks i is less than 3, so it runs, fires, and then i grows on its own until it equals 3.", "Start with i at 0, each round fires and pushes i forward by one, so after three fires the condition becomes false.", "Since i begins at zero and the limit is three, the loop counts up by itself and gives exactly three shots.", "The value i keeps increasing automatically every time the body runs, so it fires at 0, 1, 2 and then ends."]}

sentences: First i is 0, then after one fire it moves ahead, then second fire, then third fire, and when i reaches 3 it stops.
The while checks i is less than 3, so it runs, fires, and then i grows on its own until it equals 3.
Start with i at 0, each round fires and pushes i forward by one, so after three fires the condition becomes false.
Since i begins at zero and the limit is three, the loop counts up by itself and gives exactly three shots.
The value i keeps increasing automatically every time the body runs, so it fires at 0, 1, 2 and then ends.
